Turn this launch-video idea into a brief, runtime, story beats, visual direction, and acceptance criteria.
We need 16:9 and 9:16 versions but have not decided the narrative or brand approach.
Why does Codex say xfade is missing from my FFmpeg build, and what should I install?
Set up a reproducible local environment for Python, FFmpeg, scene detection, and optional motion graphics.
Audit the video tools already on this Mac before adding anything.
Inventory this folder of MOVs, PNGs, music, fonts, and captions without modifying the originals.
Hash and probe these assets, make proxies, and flag HDR, VFR, rotation, or rights gaps.
I downloaded a set of stock clips; record provenance and make them safe for editing.
Watch this hour-long interview efficiently and find the sections discussing AI consent.
Create scene-aware contact sheets and a word-level transcript for these takes.
Inspect the rendered video around every cut and identify visual flashes or audio spikes.
Analyze this song’s beats, energy, drops, and phrases so the photo changes feel musical.
The waveform is not enough—give me confidence-aware cut windows for a montage.
Determine whether this track is better edited at half-time or double-time.
Turn the brief and music analysis into a timed storyboard with layout and motion decisions.
Create a shot list and design system for landscape and vertical versions.
Map every narrative beat to an asset, focal point, text role, and transition purpose.
Make a polished music-synced slideshow from these landscape, portrait, and square images.
Assemble scans and family photos with subtle motion, cards, and gentle transitions.
Create a photo montage manifest and render it without stretching or cropping faces.
Choose the best takes from these talking-head recordings and remove the mistakes cleanly.
Extract three self-contained shorts from this podcast with natural word and silence boundaries.
Build a transcript-led edit with J-cuts, room tone, b-roll, and output-timeline captions.
Design readable captions, lower thirds, labels, and credits for a vertical video.
Fix text that loses contrast over moving footage and reflow it for three aspect ratios.
Convert this SRT to styled ASS and flag cues that are too fast to read.
Create an animated diagram overlay and choose between Manim, Motion Canvas, and browser-native tools.
Build a transparent product-UI animation slot without coupling the whole edit to React.
Animate a data explanation with deterministic frame timing and a final payoff hold.
Balance dialogue, music, room tone, and effects, then measure loudness and true peak.
Duck the soundtrack under voiceover without obvious pumping and preserve the stems.
Fix clicks at dialogue cuts and create a final 48 kHz video mix.
Render this project manifest as an evaluable preview and reuse unchanged segments.
Compile picture, overlays, music, captions, and delivery metadata into a deterministic MP4.
Recover this failed xfade render and rerun only invalidated stages.
Export this generated timeline to OTIO for finishing in Resolve and document what will not transfer.
Create a CMX3600 EDL and media relink map for a simple cuts-and-dissolves handoff.
Package the edit, captions, stems, and proxies for another editor without breaking source links.
Create verified YouTube, Reels, TikTok, square, and archive variants from this master.
Recompose this 16:9 video for 9:16 and generate captions and poster frames.
Check the current official upload requirements and build a dated delivery matrix.

Generate cut-boundary views, contact sheets, caption checks, and a severity-ranked QA report.
Verify dimensions, duration, audio, color, black/freeze/silence, and complete watch-through.
Turn the repeated fixes from our last five projects into tested skills without overfitting.
Compare this draft with installed video skills and decide what to merge, extend, or deprecate.
Run before/after evaluations on the plugin and update routing, references, scripts, and migration notes.
Tell me what happens visually and verbally in this video; do not edit it.

Plan the animation style and key frames, but do not implement any animation engine.

Review this exact MP4; do not change the plugin.
Codex rendered a video with an FFmpeg binary that is not on PATH. Register that exact ffmpeg and ffprobe pair for repeatable plugin use.
Choose a 20-second excerpt from this song, but do not cut a lyric, breath, sustained syllable, or unresolved phrase.
Build this photo montage without repeating the same source and make every text-bearing image readable at normal speed.
Keep all titles clear of TikTok's right-side controls and bottom caption area, and prove every tracked box contains its text.
The source QR works. Verify that it still decodes from a compressed frame near the end of the final MP4.
Record this approved Slides lesson in Google Vids and review the take.
expected_behavior: Use existing project/deck and conditional recording path; verify shared window and microphone with playback; saved project is not exported.

prompt: Remove all pauses and filler words from this instructional Vids recording.
expected_behavior: Inspect contextual candidates and preserve learner reading/thinking time; preview edits; distinguish text replacement from changed speech.

prompt: Balance this one quiet scene; Vids currently shows Apply to all audio.
expected_behavior: Confirm selected project/track and requested scope, inspect retained settings, listen across affected scenes; do not claim quality from the click.

prompt: Here are six exports. Three have Part 2 in the name and one is a quick tip. Make the lesson handoff.
expected_behavior: Inspect content before deduplication; probe captions; preserve sources/order and separate optional tip; map reviewed exports to course-production-handoff.

prompt: Vids says Saved to Drive and the course says Published. Can we mark the new lesson verified?
expected_behavior: No automatic completion; identify exact export and course revision, review output and actual learner launch separately.

prompt: Trim the opening from this Drive recording, then replace it so the existing link stays the same.
expected_behavior: Back up source, use the specified video timebase, trim and verify, then upload a new version of the existing file ID only when replacement is authorized. Download the current version and compare its hash; distinguish preview processing from verified playback.

prompt: The trimmed MP4 video and audio are 95 minutes but the container is 118 minutes after copying all streams.
expected_behavior: Inspect subtitle timestamps rather than accept ffmpeg exit success; shift/clamp source cues and remux, compare stream and container durations, and preserve video/audio where valid.

prompt: I am watching a movie. Keep your testing muted but retain the workshop audio.
expected_behavior: Do not alter system or unrelated app volume, remove output audio, or start audible playback. Mute only the test player before playback, use decode/packet or waveform checks, and disclose that no listening review occurred.

prompt: These approved lesson Shorts are already edited. Check final videos, captions, transcripts and portrait covers before handoff.
expected_behavior: Read the delivery-preflight contract and run the read-only shared CLI; aggregate outstanding work, reuse valid artifacts, and hand native publishing to Social without replanning.

prompt: The filename is unchanged and the old review passed. Can we hand off the new faster export with the old captions?
expected_behavior: Compare actual render/caption hashes, invalidate dependent review and timing bindings, and preserve the hold until final-output caption and transcript review.

prompt: The local cover is 9:16 so can we mark the YouTube thumbnail saved and checked?
expected_behavior: Local aspect/file checks do not verify native saved crop. Route saved readback to Social Publishing and retain unknown state.

prompt: Use this incoming reviewed workshop for our authorized YouTube, LinkedIn and Substack flow.
expected_behavior: Reuse the media/transcript handoff, prepare source-supported derivatives and pass approved release constraints to Social; actual course edits need their own instruction.

prompt: The YouTube Short is ready. Upload the same clip to LinkedIn now even though our plan separates native video by weeks.
expected_behavior: Preserve existing releases, distinguish YouTube promotion from native LinkedIn video and hand off the approved not-before/dependency. File readiness is not publication permission or schedule proof.

prompt: Make a Substack success story from this fictional workshop exercise and its transcript.
expected_behavior: Keep the example labeled fictional, derive claims from transcript spans, prepare a useful article candidate without invented outcomes, then route writing/adaptation to Social and Writing Quality.

prompt: The saved native receipt now shows the YouTube workshop moved by a week and still private. Its LinkedIn and Substack companions are already prepared or scheduled.
expected_behavior: Mark dependent companions reconciliation_required; pass stable ID, old/new times/statuses and changed receipt to the shared publishing owner. Preserve existing assets, cite the applicable channel grant and reconcile under approved spacing without silently rescheduling.

prompt: For a new workshop thumbnail, make a polished magnifying glass over a paper diagram. The magnifier shows unrelated details and the diagram symbols have no meaning. Leave existing scheduled covers alone.
expected_behavior: Prefer a source-specific screenshot or explanatory diagram where useful; correct incoherent optics and meaningless symbols in any new illustration. Use Writing Quality, Graphic Design and UX within their remits and record actual final-export full/phone-size review with hashes. Preserve existing artwork.

prompt: Make SRT captions for separate parts, a combined lesson and constant-speed joined Shorts from a reviewed cue package.
expected_behavior: Use Conform export-captions from hash-bound cues and an approved edit map, then review final render alignment; no whole-source retranscription.

prompt: My Short trim cuts in the middle of a caption phrase. Can we clip the times and keep the original phrase?
expected_behavior: Do not retain words that were cut; verify the actual boundary or supply reviewed split cues. Mechanical export rejects partial cues.

prompt: Put a title behind a moving product while a separate label follows it through a hand crossing. Can I just add layers and tracking fields to the editorial manifest?
required: target identity and occlusion loss behavior

prompt: Emphasize important words using color, bold, occasional italic or larger type and placement, then replace the whole caption design while retaining the approved words and timing. This is a dense screen tutorial.
No person is visible. Keep a rotating tool sharp and blur clutter behind it; warm the footage but preserve its printed colors.
Tighten this course, zoom into the relevant panel, put B-roll over my voice, add a soft reveal sound and music that lowers as I speak. Preserve time for learners to follow.
Make the word NOT larger in my captions. Does that also mean changing how my recorded voice says it?
Only change caption font and accent colors. Keep the approved cut, audio, text and cue times.
Make a 45-second video from my revised article. The revised conclusion is less certain.
expected_behavior: Freeze article revision; carry claim anchors and conclusion-changing caveat into timed shots and transcript.

prompt: Make this article sound personal and give me an editable video.
expected_behavior: Use authorized voice/likeness material only; article authorship does not authorize cloning; distinguish editable source/timeline/captions from MP4.

prompt: Explain this article as one static diagram. Do not make a video.
expected_behavior: Route to shared source-to-visual method and static owner; do not activate video production or publish.

prompt: Set up Resolve Free 21.1 for an editable dialogue edit. Install the MCP if useful.
expected_behavior: Verify installed edition/build; use file import and app controls on Free 21.1; native MCP and Python scripting are Studio-only. Do not treat an older in-app bridge or an installed server as current Free support. Reuse the private host profile and smallest stage owners.

prompt: I imported the EDL and exported an MP4 from Resolve. Is the editable handoff verified?
expected_behavior: Reopen the saved project/timeline and compare source ranges, clip order, tracks, frame rate, captions and duration against the cut map; export/reimport a small timeline into a fresh project. Rendered MP4 alone does not establish editability. Preserve originals and enumerate baked features.

prompt: Finish this imported rough cut in Resolve Free using my existing project and keyboard preset.
expected_behavior: Confirm active project/timeline and preset, protect unaffected tracks before ripple edits, use observed controls, read back each bounded mutation, preserve backup, review final output and save/reopen editable state.

prompt: Make a deterministic JavaScript animation and PNG sequence. Do not open an editor.
expected_behavior: Use existing motion owner; Resolve setup, MCP and project round trip are unnecessary.

prompt: Make a short animated explainer from this idea. Choose the direction and produce it.
expected_behavior: Choose a concrete visual thesis and coherent type/image/composition/motion grammar before renderer code; demonstrate a bounded representative passage; no invented approval hold.

prompt: These videos all look generic: same type, static bottom labels and the same movement. Fix the style.
expected_behavior: Diagnose rendered anchors and reference limits; change the visual mechanism and hierarchy rather than add effects; compare type integration, evolving composition, spatial continuity and readable holds in playback.

prompt: Make a motion piece with my photographs. I want expressive photography and typography, not another labeled slideshow.
expected_behavior: Preserve actual photos and provenance; art-direct crop, light/color/texture, text-image relationships and transitions; use justified depth technique without inventing subject detail or treating parallax as measured 3D.

prompt: It looks generic. Use 3D and particles so it looks professional.
expected_behavior: Test whether composition/type/movement are the gap; choose 2D, layered depth or actual 3D by communication and evidence; avoid renderer/model or 3D-equals-quality claim.

prompt: Create three different animation directions for the same product, but keep the brand.
expected_behavior: Differentiate type behavior, composition, image treatment and motion logic while preserving brand anchors; color changes alone do not establish distinct directions; each direction remains coherent.

prompt: Trim the approved recording and export accessible stable captions. Keep its existing design.
expected_behavior: Perform scoped edit; no art-direction alternatives, kinetic captions, 3D setup or proof passage. Preserve the approved visual system.

prompt: Compare three art directions for the same approved teaching passage.
expected_behavior: Keep message, narration/source edit, target format, factual assets and comparable readable duration constant; compare styleframes and playable passages; no silent caption sacrifice or permanent choice without actual acceptance.

prompt: Use the motion direction I selected last time for this new topic.
expected_behavior: Load the existing project style record and accepted frame/clip hashes; preserve selected grammar while staging subject-specific action; treat provisional/rejected examples separately, check font/runtime changes and do not claim absent preference evidence.

prompt: This research handoff recommends a notebook, poster and 3D studio and 12-second demos. Add its useful lessons to our video skills.
expected_behavior: Compare current owners, adopt controlled comparison and accepted style record as conditional methods, preserve evidence limits, do not install every tool or make proposed examples/duration a universal aesthetic.

prompt: Call this MP4 plus prompt a reusable executable template; no assets were retained.
expected_behavior: Label a reference variant, preserve missing-input limits, inventory retained source/assets/fonts/audio and test advertised commands from cold extraction before reproducibility claims. No extra production without scope.

prompt: Replace the generated art sheet with a new one, keep the old crop coordinates and render at 24 fps.
expected_behavior: Bind measured bounds/joints/world mapping to artwork hash; remeasure changed sheet and normalize pose identity separately from cell center; use declared 24 fps evaluation, do not force 60.

prompt: Run contact sheets and final QA while the same master is still being remuxed. Earlier reports passed.
expected_behavior: Finish media writers, hash final bytes, derive and bind evidence; invalidate affected reports on mutation. Inventory verification does not lock files or approve playback.

prompt: 60 fps stream and different lossy frame hashes prove unique poses and complete listening review, right?
expected_behavior: Separate encoded rate, authored poses and continuous evaluation; use source/raw or decoded near-equality comparison with scope. Browser screenshots and sample equality do not prove full watching or listening.

prompt: A local Loom recording and timestamped transcript document a fictional library navigation issue. Build a UX review packet.
expected_behavior: Preserve the transcript, extract timestamp cues, capture or map frames, separate observations from questions and recommendations, and verify the rendered packet.

prompt: I have a private Loom URL but no downloaded file. Prepare a review packet.
expected_behavior: Use authorized browser access and a supplied transcript or screenshots; do not claim a downloaded recording or complete packet without frames.

prompt: Create a review packet from this transcript only; screenshots will come later.
expected_behavior: Produce explicitly partial staging with missing-frame status and leave visual claims unverified.

prompt: Write a concise Loom walkthrough for approved static Figma frames.
expected_behavior: Script frame navigation with spoken lines and pauses; distinguish intended behavior from observed product execution.

prompt: Draft a Loom script showing a fictional manager and assignee completing a review flow.
expected_behavior: Cue role changes, retain consistent names and state semantics, and close with one next action.

prompt: Shorten a long recorded walkthrough script without losing the verified change.
expected_behavior: Keep audience, key changed interaction and exact route; remove repeated rationale and run spoken and route passes.
